summary_en.motivation: To develop a micromechanics model for predicting the mechanical properties of metallic alloys fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: A homogenization approach based on microstructural features such as grain morphology and texture was employed.
summary_en.result: The model successfully predicts elastic moduli and anisotropy consistent with experimental observations.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by comparing model predictions with experimental data from the literature.

papers.title: Mid-term results of revision total hip arthroplasty with an uncemented modular femoral component
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: During revision total hip arthroplasty (THA), the surgeon commonly faces deficient proximal femoral bone. In this situation, distal fixation of the prosthesis is required. The aim of the current retrospective study is to assess the clinical and radiographic mid-term outcome of revision total hip arthroplasty using a modular uncemented, tapered, grit-blasted, distal straight stem system. METHODS: This retrospective study included 70 femoral revisions that were performed in 67 patients using the device of interest. All patients were operated on via an extended trochanteric osteotomy. 60 revisions were performed as 1-stage (12 infected) and 10 as 2-stage (all infected) revisions. At 3 months postoperatively and at final follow-up, patients were assessed radiographically for the presence of osteolysis and for distal integration. RESULTS: The mean follow-up time was 4.3 (2.0-7.6) years. 4 patients had a removal of at least 1 prosthetic component. Stem survival for any reason was 92% after 5 years (95% confidence interval [CI], 83%-100%). With aseptic loosening of the stem as the endpoint of interest, survival after 5 years was 96% (95% CI, 88%-100%). A postoperative subsidence rate of 14.7% was found. No perioperative femoral fractures were found in the current patient series. CONCLUSIONS: This study showed excellent mid-term survival and good clinical and radiographic outcomes in patients who had undergone revision THA with a modular uncemented, tapered, straight design.

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate mid-term clinical and radiographic outcomes of revision THA with a modular uncemented femoral stem.
summary_en.method: A retrospective study of 70 femoral revisions using extended trochanteric osteotomy and clinical/radiographic follow-up.

papers.title: Bioprinting-Based PDLSC-ECM Screening for in Vivo Repair of Alveolar Bone Defect Using Cell-Laden, Injectable and Photocrosslinkable Hydrogels
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is an inflammatory disease worldwide that may result in periodontal defect (especially alveolar bone defect) and even tooth loss. Stem-cell-based approach combined with injectable hydrogels has been proposed as a promising strategy in periodontal treatments. Stem cells fate closely depends on their extracellular matrix (ECM) characteristics. Hence, it is necessary to engineer an appropriate injectable hydrogel to deliver stem cells into the defect while serving as the ECM during healing. Therefore, stem cell-ECM interaction should be studied for better stem cell transplantation. In this study, we developed a bioprinting-based strategy to study stem cell-ECM interaction and thus screen an appropriate ECM for in vivo repair of alveolar bone defect. Periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs) were encapsulated in injectable, photocrosslinkable composite hydrogels composed of gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) and poly(ethylene glycol) dimethacrylate (PEGDA). PDLSC-laden GelMA/PEGDA hydrogels with varying composition were efficiently fabricated via a 3D bioprinting platform by controlling the volume ratio of GelMA-to-PEGDA. PDLSC behavior and fate were found to be closely related to the engineered ECM composition. The 4/1 GelMA/PEGDA composite hydrogel was selected since the best performance in osteogenic differentiation in vitro. Finally, in vivo study indicated a maximal and robust new bone formation in the defects treated with the PDLSC-laden hydrogel with optimized composition as compared to the hydrogel alone and the saline ones. The developed approach would be useful for studying cell-ECM interaction in 3D and paving the way for regeneration of functional tissue.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及生物打印用于骨修复，但完全不包含人工智能或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is purely a biological material screening and in vivo validation study.

summary_zh.motivation: 探寻适合牙槽骨修复的干细胞-细胞外基质生物墨水组合。
summary_zh.method: 通过3D生物打印制备不同配比的GelMA/PEGDA水凝胶包裹牙周膜干细胞，筛选最佳成骨分化条件。
summary_zh.result: 4/1 GelMA/PEGDA水凝胶在体外促进成骨分化，体内实现最大新骨形成。
summary_zh.validation: 体外成骨分化实验和体内大鼠牙槽骨缺损模型验证。

summary_en.motivation: To identify an optimal hydrogel composition for stem cell delivery in alveolar bone repair by studying cell-ECM interactions via bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Periodontal ligament stem cells were encapsulated in photocrosslinkable GelMA/PEGDA hydrogels with varying ratios, fabricated by a 3D bioprinting platform.
summary_en.result: The 4/1 GelMA/PEGDA hydrogel promoted osteogenic differentiation in vitro and achieved maximal new bone formation in vivo.
summary_en.validation: Validation through in vitro osteogenic assays and in vivo rat alveolar bone defect models.
